program.help:
Downsample a .dat file to create the LFP file.
If <session>-spkclean.dat already exists (produced by a prior run of ndm_stripdat), it is used as the resampling source instead of the raw .dat. The LFP will therefore be spike-free without any extra configuration.
The subtractSpikes parameter controls what happens when no cleaned dat is present:
auto Run ndm_stripdat first if .spk.N files exist (default). yes Always run ndm_stripdat; error if .spk.N files are missing. no Resample from the raw .dat unconditionally.
When ndm_lfp invokes ndm_stripdat internally, the cleaned dat is removed once the LFP file has been written. If you ran ndm_stripdat manually beforehand, ndm_lfp leaves that file in place for ndm_redetectspikes or other downstream use.
PARAMETERS
# samplingRate
Target LFP sampling rate in Hz (default = 1250 Hz).
# subtractSpikes
Whether to subtract spike waveforms before resampling (see above). All subtraction parameters (redetectSpikes etc.) are controlled via ndm_stripdat.
# inputExtension
Data file read for resampling, without the leading dot (default dat). Point it at an alternative, externally-processed source (e.g. car.dat) to downsample that file instead of the raw recording.
Any value but dat selects the source outright: the spike-cleaned dat is not used even when present, because ndm_stripdat cleans <session>.dat and cannot produce a spike-free version of another file. Combining it with subtractSpikes=yes is refused rather than silently resolved one way or the other.
